about: The tools the Airia MCP gateway built from arii.yaml, read back from an MCP deployment's cached tools (GET /v1/McpDeployments/{id}, cachedTools), beside the operation each was built from, taken from a Redocly bundle of the same commit. Read-only; nothing was uploaded.

operation.description:
Resolves marker names to marker type IDs.

Use when you have a marker name and need its ID before calling another marker tool.

Supports up to 200 keywords. Matching is case-insensitive substring matching against
names, aliases, and lab component names. It is not fuzzy matching and does not apply
synonyms.

Use the clinical marker name rather than the user's wording when possible: `my sugar`
matches nothing where `glucose` and `hba1c` do; `bp` returns IGFBP-3, so send
`blood pressure`. A device is not a marker — "my rings" is an Oura ring, whose
markers are Readiness Score and Sleep Score. Send every candidate form in the one
call; keywords cost nothing and a marker you fail to find costs the answer.

If the same marker name exists for different specimens, the results distinguish them
by type — `Ferritin` is both Serum and Blood, `Glucose` both Blood and Urine. Pick
the specimen the question implies.

Results are keyed by the keyword you sent. An empty array for a keyword means the
catalog has no such marker — it does not mean the patient has no data for it. Do not
report absence from this tool.

keywords.description: Search keywords (up to 200). Send every form the question needs in one call.

tenantId.description: Optional tenant/group ID (GUID) to filter by.

includeDefault.description: Whether to include default (null tenant) marker types.

operation.description:
Returns what a person is currently taking — medications and supplements together
— one row per item, including display name, form, strength, dose quantity,
schedule, instructions, and today's dose logs.

Use for the current medication or supplement list.

`type` is optional. Omit it for both categories, or pass `Medication` or
`Supplement` for one. Omitting it does not default to medications.

Returns only items active today. An item that is on hold, completed or stopped,
or whose schedule has not started or has already ended, is not returned.

Strength is `strengthValue` with `strengthUnitCode`, a free-text unit code that
can carry a concentration such as `mg/mL`. Always report the two together.

`todayHistory` holds today's dose logs for the item. An empty `todayHistory` does
not mean nothing was scheduled: a day's logs exist only once the prescription was
created or updated, so today's rows may not have been created yet.

For whether a dose was taken on an earlier day, use `get_dose_history`.

If this read fails, say you could not retrieve the data. A failure is never
evidence that the person has none.

operation.description:
Returns counts of a person's doses by outcome — `total`, `taken`, `skipped`,
`missed` and `pending` — plus `adherenceRate` as a percentage.

Use when the question is how well someone is keeping to their doses, rather than
reading every dose through `get_dose_history` and counting them.

`type` is optional. Omit it for one figure covering medications and supplements
combined, or pass `Medication` or `Supplement` for a single category.

`startDate` and `endDate` are both optional and neither is defaulted. The window
applies to the day each dose was scheduled for. Send both whenever the question is
about a period ("this month", "since starting X"); send neither only when the
question is about the person's whole history, because that is what you get back.

Omitting `endDate` leaves the window open-ended, so doses that are not yet due are
counted as well. Those land in `pending`.

`adherenceRate` is `taken` divided by `total` minus `pending`. It is reported as 0
when nothing in the window has resolved yet, so check `total` and `pending` before
describing a rate of 0 as poor adherence.

A skipped dose counts against the rate exactly as a missed one does, even though
the person chose to skip it.

If this read fails, say you could not retrieve the data. A failure is never
evidence that the person has none.

operation.description:
Returns every medication or supplement on a person's record, current and past,
whatever its status — `Active`, `OnHold`, `Completed`, `Stopped`, `Superseded`
or `EnteredInError` — with `deactivatedAt` for anything no longer in use.

Use for what someone used to take, when they stopped, or whether they have been
on a drug before. For what they are taking now, use
`get_active_medications_and_supplements`.

`type` must always be sent. It accepts `Medication` or `Supplement`, and omitting
it returns medications only, with a 200 and nothing saying supplements were left
out. Call the tool twice when both categories are needed.

Read `status` on every row. This tool returns discontinued and mistakenly entered
items alongside current ones, so presenting the rows as a medication list would
overstate what the person takes.

If this read fails, say you could not retrieve the data. A failure is never
evidence that the person has none.

operation.description:
Returns the individual scheduled doses of a person's medications and supplements,
grouped by the day each dose was scheduled for, with its status: `Pending`,
`Taken`, `Skipped`, or `Missed`.

Use for medication or supplement adherence, and to determine whether a dose was
taken.

This is not the current medication list. Use
`get_active_medications_and_supplements` for that.

`type` is optional. Omit it for both categories, or pass `Medication` or
`Supplement` for one.

`endDate` defaults to today in the person's own timezone.

Use a `pageSize` of 50 normally. A page holds at most that many doses, newest
scheduled dose first. `pageNumber` is 0-based. When `hasNextPage` is `true`, more
doses exist in the window; ask for the next page only if the question needs
older doses. For counts and adherence rates, use `get_adherence_stats` instead
of paging through every dose.

`dateFilterBy` defaults to `ScheduledDate`, which keeps each dose in the day it
was due. Pass `EffectiveDate` to window taken doses by when they were actually
taken instead.

`yyyy-MM-dd` works on both axes, and the end day is covered in full. A UTC instant
such as `2026-08-28T00:00:00Z` is also accepted and is used exactly as sent.

`Pending` means a dose is still due and `Missed` means it is past its grace
period. The endpoint reconciles the two before answering, so both can be reported
as read.

If this read fails, say you could not retrieve the data. A failure is never
evidence that the person has none.

operation.description:
Returns a trend for each named marker, one row per marker **and source**, the
person's preferred source first (AIP-350).

**Use this for any trend or "compared to usual" question.** It returns the averages
with the arithmetic already done: `direction` (`Up`, `Down` or `Flat`, from a
straight-line fit over every daily value, `Flat` when the change is smaller than the
marker's own trend threshold) and `change` (in the marker's unit). Report those; do
not work the trend out yourself.

Each row has `markerTypeId`, `displayName`, `unit`, `dataSourceName`,
`isPreferredSource`, `dailyAverage`, `weekdayAverage`, `weekendAverage`,
`highestSingleDay`, `lowestRange`, `highestRange`, `readingDays` (days with a value),
`firstRecordDate`, `lastRecordDate`, `direction`, `change`, `goalType`, `goalMinValue`, `goalMaxValue`,
`daysMeetingGoal`, `daysMissingGoal`, `baselineAverage`, `displayPrecision` and
`referenceRange` — the range on that source's newest reading in the window that
carries one, absent when none does. Every number is already rounded to
`displayPrecision`.

`lastRecordDate` earlier than the window's end means that source stopped sending:
say so. A source with no value in the window has no row.

**Options:**
- `groupBy=Week` or `groupBy=Month` — adds `periods`, one average per calendar week
  (Monday to Sunday) or month, each with its `readingDays`. A period's `periodStart`
  and `periodEnd` are its first and last days with a value, not the week's or month's
  bounds. Use it for "month by month" and for any window longer than a few weeks.
- `baselineDays=N` — adds `baselineAverage` over the N days before
  `recordStartDate`, from the same source. "Compared to usual" in one call: a 30-day
  window with `baselineDays=90` compares the month with the 90 days before it.
- Goals: compare `dailyAverage` with the inclusive `goalMinValue` and `goalMaxValue`.
  A missing side is open. `goalType` is Range, SpecificValue (equal bounds),
  MinimumThreshold (minimum only), or MaximumThreshold (maximum only).
  A value is inside when it satisfies every supplied bound; otherwise it is below
  the minimum or above the maximum. Describe a Range goal as a range, never one target.
  For example, 450 minutes is inside a 420–540-minute sleep goal (7–9 hours).
  `daysMeetingGoal` and `daysMissingGoal` count days for floors, ceilings and ranges.
  Both are null for a SpecificValue target, which has no better side.
  Goal metadata is null when no goal or unit conversion applies; do not grade that row.
- `select=Changing` — only rows whose `direction` is `Up` or `Down`.
- `includeChart=true` — adds `chartData`, one `{recordDate, value}` per day with a
  value. **Off by default. Turn it on only to draw a chart.**
- `dataSources` — read only these sources.

`specificMarkers` is required, 1–20 ids, from `get_user_marker_types_with_data`.
`recordStartDate` and `recordEndDate` are both required as `yyyy-MM-dd`. No value is
carried forward from before the window. Not paged.

On a share-based read the start date may be narrowed to the share's own window, so
the range covered can be shorter than the one you asked for, with nothing on the
response saying so. The baseline stops at the share's start too, so `baselineAverage`
can cover fewer than `baselineDays` days. Read the returned dates rather than assuming
your range held.

If this read fails, say you could not retrieve the data. A failure is never evidence
that the person has none.

parameters.description:

operation.description:
Returns a person's current marker values, one row per marker **and source**, on a
row trimmed to fourteen fields, together with the category counts for the window.

**Every source.** The app shows one source per marker. This read returns every
source that has a value in the window — Apple Health, Oura, Mira, the person's own
entries — each on its own row, the person's preferred source first. So a marker the
preferred source has nothing for still comes back, from the source that has it. Cite
each row by its own `dataSourceName` (AIP-350).

**This is the default read for an open question about how someone is doing.** For
goals, use `get_marker_averages_compact`, whose rows carry them.

Each row has `markerTypeId`, `displayName`, `value`, `unit`, `recordDate`,
`categoryName`, `dataSourceName`, `isPreferredSource`, `aggregationMethod`, and —
where a reference range applies — `rangeStatus`, `outOfRange` and `referenceRange`,
the range the value was judged against, in the row's `unit`. A row that was not
judged has no `referenceRange`. `secondValue` and `textValue` carry blood-pressure
style pairs and non-numeric results.

`value` is the window's value by `aggregationMethod`: with `Average` or `Sum` it is
the average or total over the whole window, dated by the newest reading behind it.
Only `Latest` is a single reading. No value is carried forward from before the
window: for "when was X last measured", use `select=Stale`.

`rangeStatus` is the side of the normal band the row's value is on: `L` below, `H`
above, `InRange` inside, null when no range could judge it (null never means normal).
The range is the lab report's own when the reading carries one, else the range
resolved for this patient — the same judgement `get_out_of_range_results` makes. For
the range's source and the draw date, call `get_out_of_range_results`.

**Not paged.** Every matching row comes back. Scope the call: pass `specificMarkers`
(up to 100), `categoryId`, or a `select` other than `All`. An unscoped `select=All`
is refused with 400.

**Filters, all worked out on the server:**
- `select=Abnormal` — values outside their own reference range. Each source is
  judged on its own, so an out-of-range Oura value shows even when the preferred
  source's value is in range. Prefer it for "how am I doing": it answers over the
  whole chart in a handful of rows.
- `select=NotInPreferred` — markers the preferred source has nothing for in the
  window while another source does. The preferred source is always checked, even when
  `dataSources` leaves it out; its rows are not returned then.
- `select=Stale` with `staleDays=N` — markers whose newest reading, in any source, is
  more than N days before `recordEndDate`. Each row is that source's newest reading,
  dated, with `aggregationMethod` `Latest`. `categoryId` is refused with it, its
  rows carry no `categoryName`, and the response's `categoryFacets` is empty and
  `unclassifiedCount` is 0.
- `select=SourcesDisagree` — markers where two sources' values from the same day
  differ by more than the marker's own trend threshold. Values from different days are
  a change over time and are not compared. A marker with no trend threshold is never
  flagged.
- `dataSources` — read only these sources.
- `categoryId` — one category, taken from `categoryFacets`.

Rows come back grouped by marker, the most recently recorded marker first, and within
a marker the preferred source first. `markerCount` is the number of markers; rows
outnumber it when a marker has more than one source.

`categoryFacets` counts markers per category across the window, before `categoryId`
is applied. This is the one place a category filter works on a name you can read.
`unclassifiedCount` is how many markers no source's value could be judged for — read
it before treating a short abnormal list as "everything else was checked".

`recordStartDate` and `recordEndDate` are both required as `yyyy-MM-dd`.

`requestingUserId` is deprecated and ignored: the caller is always the session's own
identity. This read is Bearer only; under `X-API-Key` it returns 401.

`specificMarkers` entries that are unparseable or resolve to no marker type are
skipped and returned in `unmatchedIds` (AIP-236); the call is rejected only when no
entry parses at all. Entries that are real markers outside your access to this person
are returned in `withheldIds`; without `specificMarkers`, `accessRestricted: true` says
the read covered only what you may see.

On a share-based read the start date may be narrowed to the share's own window, so
the range covered can be shorter than the one you asked for, with nothing on the
response saying so. Read the returned dates rather than assuming your range held.

If this read fails, say you could not retrieve the data. A failure is never evidence
that the person has none.

came from and the reference range applicable to the patient.

For a trend over time use `get_marker_averages_compact`, and for a marker's
individual readings use `get_marker_samples_compact`.

Otherwise send at least one of `recordStartDate` or `recordEndDate` as
`yyyy-MM-dd`. Either record date can be sent alone; the missing side leaves
the range open, even with `observationId`.
Repeat `markerTypeIds` for each marker GUID to include.

`observationTypes` uses exact matching against the observation type name. The
full set is `Lab`, `DeviceTracking`, `SelfReported`, `Scan`, `Exam`, `Activity`,

individually). Say which one applied when you report the range. `cohortId` and
`cohortName` are set only when `source` is `Cohort`.

range printed on the lab report.

`hasNextPage`; `totalCount` and `totalPages` come back on the same response.

operation.description:
Returns the person's lab results that sit outside their normal band. Each one has a
server-computed `flag`: `L` means below the normal band and `H` means above it. It also
has a `severity` (`Borderline` or `OutOfRange`), the normal band's bounds
(`normalRange.min` / `normalRange.max`, where null means open on that side), the
range's source, and the draw date.

**Use this whenever you are asked to flag, list or summarise out-of-range lab
results.** It is the one read that gives, for each result, the side it is off, the
range it was judged against, where that range came from and the draw date. Band
labels on `get_observation_samples` (`segments[].label`) are alert levels, not
directions: in most ranges "Low" is the in-range green band and "High" is a red band
on either side. Never turn a band label into "low" or "high". Take the direction from
`flag` only.

`rangeSource` says whose range decided the flag. `LabReport` is the range printed on
the lab report. `Patient`, `Cohort`, `Org` (the practice) and `Platform` (the
default) are the resolved tiers; `cohortName` is set for `Cohort`. When the lab report
decided the flag and a practice or platform range also applies, that range is in
`alternateRange` with its own `flag`. Say which source you used, and give the draw
date (`drawDate`) for every flag.

`sexSpecific` is `Male` or `Female` when the band used was sex-specific. Say so.

`noRange` lists the results no range could judge, each with a `reason`:
`NoRangeDefined`, `SexUnknown` (only sex-specific bands exist and the person has no
Male/Female sex on record), `UnitMismatch`, `TextResult` or
`UnrecognizedRangeLabels`. For these, say there is no reference range to judge
against and give no flag. Never supply a range from general knowledge. A result
missing from `results` is only in range if it was counted in `inRangeCount`.

When `accessRestricted` is true, your access to this person covers only some marker
types, so lab results outside it were never read. An empty or short `results` then
does not mean nothing is out of range: say the check covered only the results you
are allowed to see.

`latestOnly` (default `true`) judges only each marker's most recent draw in the
window. Pass `false` to judge every draw, for "has this been high before". Both
dates are optional. Omit them to judge every result on file; `recordEndDate` before
`recordStartDate` returns 400. When `truncated` is true the read stopped at its
sample cap. Narrow the window, and say the list may be incomplete.

`documentId` is the uploaded lab report the result was extracted from (null for
results from a connector). `observationId` is the lab panel and `sampleId` the result.

Omit `requestingUserId` under Bearer/passthrough: the session identifies the caller
and any value sent is discarded. On the legacy `X-API-Key` path it is still the
caller's identity.

On a share-based read the start date may be narrowed to the share's own window.

If this read fails, say you could not check the results against their ranges and
flag nothing. A failure is never evidence that the results are normal.

Returns the marker types that have at least one sample in the user's complete
history.

about.** It is the only tool that says which markers this person actually has, so it
is what turns a name in a question into an id you can safely ask for. It applies to a
patient you are reading as a clinician exactly as it does to yourself: access is
resolved from who is asking, and no header is involved.

has, call this with `tags=labresult`, then read the ids in groups of up to 20 with

`totalCount`, the number of entries in the window. Not paged: the list is the whole

has an end; for duration-only records, `endDate` is `startDate` plus `duration`.

caller's identity, and omitting it there returns 400 "RequestingUserId parameter is

tool.name: arii_mcp_list_notes
tool.description:
Returns clinical notes for a provider.

Use `patientId` to scope the results to a specific patient. Without it, the tool
may return notes across the tenant and the results may belong to unrelated
patients.

Patients should use `get_shared_notes` instead.

`pageNumber` is 0-based and `pageSize` is 1-100, default 20. Outside that range
returns 400.

This is the v1 shape, where a note's `date` is a full timestamp. The v2 route
returns the same fields with `date` as a calendar day; the catalog stays on v1
deliberately so the tool contract does not change under agents mid-flight.

isPrivate.description: Filter by the note's private flag. Omit to return both private and non-private notes.

patientId.description:
The patient's Arii user ID (`UserDto.id` GUID) — not an Airia profile ID.
**Always set this.** Without it the call reaches across the tenant.

operation.description:
Returns events in a user's record over a date range, such as lab panels, scans,
workouts, and self-reports. Includes event type, date, and source.

Use to find or identify observations. Use marker tools for the measurements
inside an observation.

Use `RecordStartDate` and/or `RecordEndDate` as `yyyy-MM-dd`. Either date can be
used alone.

Do not omit the date range to work around an error. Without a range, the tool
returns the most recent rows, which may answer a different question.

`PageNumber` is 0-based and `PageSize` is 1-100, default 10.

**For how many, quote `totalCount`.** It counts every observation matching the
request, across all pages. A page holds at most `PageSize` rows, so counting the
rows comes out short as soon as there is a second page, and a long page is easy to
miscount.

**Never set `IncludeHealthKitSamples=true`.** It returns every measurement inside
every matching event. One lab panel came back at 288,000 characters; a ten-panel
request was rejected outright for exceeding the context window. For underlying
samples use `get_observation_samples`.

`MarkerTypeIds` narrows the result to the observations that carry those marker
types, which is the cheap way to find the panel a named marker came from. Pass
`markerTypeId` values, and leave `IncludeHealthKitSamples` false — this scopes which
observations come back, not how much each one carries.

Prefer the record-date pair.

parameters.name: PageNumber
parameters.description: Page number (0-based).

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Page size (1-100, default 10). Rejected outside that range.

parameters.description:

operation.description:
Searches what a user's uploaded documents say and returns the matching passages.

Use to read or quote a document on the selected user's file — a lab report, a letter,
an imaging summary. This is the tool for a clinician reading a patient's documents:
the data store search tools only ever see the uploads of the person chatting, so on a
clinician's turn they return the clinician's own files, never the patient's.

The search runs as the selected user, so it returns that user's files and no one
else's. The caller must be allowed to read that user's records; a caller who is not
gets 403 and no search runs.

Each passage carries its `text`, a similarity `score`, and the document it came from:
`documentId`, `documentName`, `uploadedAt` and `downloadUrl`. Quote the passage text
and cite the document by name. A passage from an uploaded note has no `documentId`
and carries the stored file name.

An empty list means nothing matched the query in that user's documents. It does not
mean the user has no documents — `get_user_documents` lists those. Search again with
the clinical term rather than the user's wording before reporting that a document does
not mention something.

To search one document, call `get_user_documents` first and pass its `id` in
`documentIds`. Ids that do not belong to the selected user are ignored; when none
belong to them, nothing is searched and the list is empty.

Does not return extracted lab values. To read a lab's numbers as data use the marker
tools.

selectedUserId.description: Arii user ID whose documents to search. Not an Airia profile ID.

query.description: The search text. Use the clinical term — "ferritin", not "my iron".

documentIds.description: Optional. Document IDs from `get_user_documents` to search within; all of the user's documents when omitted.
